reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus (NVA5-NVA7) publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across 1.18 million square feet of technical space. At 100 kW per rack, a typical density for hyperscale AI work, this amounts to roughly 1,160 racks. At 8 GPUs per rack, a common AI training configuration, the campus could hold approximately 9,280 accelerators at full utilization, though the operator publishes no tenant or workload details.

The campus holds environmental and energy certifications: ISO 14001 for environmental management, ISO 50001 for energy management, and NWF Certified Wildlife Habitat status. These certifications describe the campus as built to manage its environmental footprint but do not indicate AI workload or customer type.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish capacity figures totaling 1,375 MW. The Sterling campus ranks 24th among Virginia's published figures, falling outside the top tier of state capacity. It represents 8.4 percent of Virginia's published IT megawatt total, placing it as a significant but not dominant regional asset.
